portion_doctrine: Segments 81-90 comprise two major instructional videos: (1) LangChain crash course covering agents, memory, multimodal input, RAG, and middleware patterns; (2) RAG-from-scratch series by Lance Martin covering indexing, retrieval, generation, query translation methods (multi-query, RAG Fusion, decomposition, step-back, HyDE), routing, corrective RAG, and adaptive RAG with LangGraph. Content is primarily video transcript with code examples.
operating_rules: LangChain 1.0 unifies imports through main langchain package (not scattered across langchain_core, langchain_openai, etc.)
Load environment variables with python-dotenv before authenticating with API keys
Agent reasoning pattern: Thought -> Action -> Tool Call -> Observation -> repeat until final answer
Memory types: ConversationalBufferMemory grows endlessly; ConversationalBufferWindowMemory limits to K exchanges
Embeddings map text to fixed-length vectors (e.g., 1536 dims for OpenAI); semantic similarity enables document retrieval
RAG pipeline: Index -> Retrieve -> Generate. Retrieval done via K-nearest neighbor in embedding space (similarity search)
Query translation improves retrieval by rewriting/decomposing user questions before indexing
Routing directs questions to correct data source (vector store, graph DB, relational DB, web search) via logical or semantic routing
Active RAG adds grading steps: check document relevance, check for hallucinations, check answer completeness; retry if needed
LangGraph state machines encode RAG workflows as nodes (functions) + edges (transitions); conditional edges implement routing logic
Structured outputs constrain LLM responses to defined schemas (e.g., yes/no binary); enables deterministic flow control
Tool binding: Convert Python function or data class to function schema; bind to LLM for structured tool use
named_methods: Multi-Query: Generate 3-5 rewritten versions of user question from different perspectives; retrieve for each; union results
RAG Fusion: Multi-query + reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) to consolidate ranked doc lists across multiple questions
Query Decomposition: Break complex question into sub-questions; solve sequentially with prior answers informing later ones; concatenate for final answer
Step-Back Prompting: Generate more abstract/general version of question using few-shot examples; retrieve docs for both concrete and abstract queries
HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings): Generate hypothetical document that would answer the question; embed and retrieve similar docs
Logical Routing: LLM classifies question into category (e.g., Python/JS/Go docs); bind to structured output schema
Semantic Routing: Embed question + embed category prompts; similarity search picks best category
Corrective RAG (CRAG): Retrieve -> Grade for relevance -> If all bad, web search -> Generate
Adaptive RAG: Query analysis + routing -> Grade retrieval relevance + fallback to web search -> Generate -> Grade for hallucinations + answer usefulness + auto-retry
Dynamic System Prompts: Use middleware to swap system prompt based on user expertise level (beginner/expert/child)
Dynamic Model Selection: Middleware swaps model based on query complexity (e.g., simple queries use GPT-4 mini, complex use GPT-4 Turbo)
Reciprocal Rank Fusion: Aggregate multiple ranked document lists; formula: 1/(k+rank), sum across lists, re-rank
numbers: OpenAI embedding model: text-embedding-3-large produces 1536-dimensional vectors
Default embedding context window: 512 to 8000 tokens (varies by model)
K-NN parameter: K=1 retrieves 1 nearest doc, K=3 retrieves 3, etc.
RAG Fusion typically generates 4 questions for reciprocal rank fusion
Step-back few-shot examples: 2-4 example pairs provided in prompt
Conversation buffer window memory: K parameter limits to last K exchanges (question-answer pairs)
Token cost: OpenAI charges ~0.002 dollars per 1000 tokens (model-dependent)
Context windows expanding: 4-8k tokens (1 year ago) -> 120k tokens (Command R) -> 1M tokens (recent models)
Adaptive RAG total latency: 6-7 seconds for full graph with grading; 1 second for LLM fallback
Corrective RAG checks relevance threshold: Binary yes/no per document
skills: Agent construction: create_agent() function + tools list + system prompt
Tool definition: @tool decorator on Python function, specify description, return_direct flag
API integration: Weather API (wtr.in), Tavily web search, SERP API for Google search
Streaming responses: model.stream() yields chunks in real-time
Structured output: Pydantic dataclass bound to LLM via with_structured_output()
LangGraph workflow: StateGraph -> add_node() -> add_edge() -> add_conditional_edges() -> compile()
Middleware hooks: before_agent, after_agent, before_model, after_model, wrap_tool_call, wrap_model_call
Embedding pipeline: load_documents() -> split_text() -> embed -> FAISS/Chroma vector store
RAG chain assembly: PromptTemplate + LLM + OutputParser chained via LangChain Expression Language (LCEL)
tools: LangChain: Python framework for agents, chains, memory, tools, middleware
LangGraph: State machine framework for complex rag/agent workflows
LangSmith: Observability platform for tracing, debugging, evaluating LLM applications
OpenAI API: GPT-4, GPT-4 mini, embedding models
Anthropic API: Claude models mentioned (context available)
Google GenAI: Access to Google models
Cohere: Command R (35B open-weight) model; supports tool use, routing, 120k context window
SERP API: Google search results API
Pydantic: Data validation via dataclasses, structured output schemas
LangChain Expression Language (LCEL): Composable chain syntax
prompts: Multi-Query: 'Your task is to generate 5 different search queries based on the following user input. These should be different perspectives.'
RAG Fusion: 'You are a helpful assistant that generates multiple search queries based on a single input.'
Decomposition: 'Given an input question, decompose it into a set of sub problems that can be solved individually.'
Step-Back: 'You are an expert. Your task is to step back and paraphrase a question to generate a more generic/abstract question that is easier to answer.'
HyDE: 'Write a paper passage to answer the given question.'
Routing (Logical): 'You are an expert at routing a user question based on [context]. Route to: [list of tools].'
Grading Relevance: 'Are the retrieved documents relevant to the user question? Binary score: yes or no.'
Grading Hallucination: 'Is the answer grounded in the facts of the retrieved documents? Binary: yes or no.'
Grading Answer Quality: 'Does the generation adequately address the user question? Binary: yes or no.'
Weather Tool: 'Return weather information for a given city.'
RAG Generation: 'Answer the following question based on this context: [context]. Question: [question].'
System Prompt (Dynamic): Varies by user role: 'Provide detailed technical responses' (expert), 'Keep explanations simple' (beginner), 'Explain as if to a 5-year-old' (child)
gates: API Key Validation: Verify OPENAI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variables set
Embedding Model Check: Confirm text-embedding-3-large or equivalent available for chosen provider
Tool Call Verification: Confirm tool calls present in LLM output before routing (fallback if missing)
Document Relevance Gate: Grade each retrieved document; filter if score below threshold
Hallucination Detection: Check if answer is grounded in retrieved documents
Answer Completeness: Verify generation addresses user question
Web Search Fallback: If vector store retrieval scores low on relevance, trigger web search
Memory Token Budget: Monitor cumulative tokens in conversation history; summarize if > 4000 tokens (summarization middleware)
Structured Output Compliance: Validate LLM response adheres to Pydantic schema before parsing
Graph State Validation: Ensure all required state dict keys present before node execution
contradictions: Memory Design: ConversationalBufferMemory (unlimited growth) vs. ConversationalBufferWindowMemory (bounded K) - trade-off between context recall and cost. Rules state to use windowed memory to manage token costs.

Retrieval Strategy: Dense (embedding-based) vs. Sparse (BM25/word frequency) retrieval. Document notes dense (ML embeddings) is 'more recently' developed and stronger; sparse remains useful for exact keyword matches.
Query Rewriting: Multi-Query (simpler, fan-out) vs. Decomposition (sequential, interleaved). Contradicts which is 'better'—depends on question complexity and domain.

Model Selection in Adaptive RAG: Command R (35B, open-weight, fast, tool-tuned) suggested for latency + routing quality. GPT-4 models (proprietary, larger, slower) may be more capable. Trade-off between cost/speed and raw capability not resolved.

Step-Back vs. Decomposition: Step-Back generates ONE abstract question; Decomposition breaks into MULTIPLE sub-questions. Conceptually opposite approaches presented as both valid for same problem class.
Routing Logic: Semantic routing (similarity to category embeddings) vs. Logical routing (LLM classification). Both presented; no guidance on when to prefer one.

Retrieval Fallback: Corrective RAG uses web search if documents fail relevance check. Adaptive RAG also uses web search on low relevance. Unclear if web search is preferred over re-ranking or rewriting query.
Middleware Timing: Hooks fire before_agent, before_model, after_model, after_agent. Order of execution and state propagation not fully detailed; could affect logic flow.
weird_gold: Agents as reasoning engines: LLMs perform chain-of-thought internally; tools provide external grounding. Agents ≠ just prompts; they decide WHEN and WHAT to call.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion formula (1/(k+rank)) elegantly combines multiple ranked lists without explicit reweighting; is information-theoretic optimal for rank aggregation.

Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE): Generate fake doc that WOULD answer question, embed it (not the question), retrieve docs similar to the fake doc. Counterintuitive but works because hypothetical doc is 'closer' to real docs in embedding space than raw question.
Memory trades token cost linearly: Each message in buffer costs tokens on every subsequent API call. Window size K multiplies cost by K. Insight: memory is expensive; choose window size carefully.
Corrective RAG insight: 'Bad retrieval' → web search fallback, not re-ranking or query rewriting. Suggests web search data diversity > query rewriting for out-of-domain questions.
State Machines (LangGraph) vs. Agents: Agents are flexible but black-box; state machines are explicit control flow. LangGraph is 'flow engineering' (architectural design before coding).

Structured Output Binding: Pydantic class -> function schema -> LLM function calling -> parser. Converts 'unstructured generation' into deterministic type-safe output. Enables graph conditional logic.
Command R tuning for RAG: 35B open-weight model outperforms larger models on routing/grading tasks when fine-tuned for tool use + RAG. Suggests domain fine-tuning > raw scale.
K-nearest neighbor retrieval assumes semantic similarity = relevant. True if documents in vector store are semantically dense; false if sparse/contradictory.
Middleware hooks pattern: Insert logic between request/response without modifying agent/model code. Enables swappable observability, rate-limiting, hallucination detection, model swapping.
Few-shot prompting in Step-Back: Providing 2-4 concrete examples of abstract reformulation helps LLM generalize to unseen questions. Example quality > quantity for prompting.
LangSmith observability: Logs every node, edge, tool call, intermediate state. Critical for debugging agentic systems where reasoning is opaque. Justifies enterprise tracing investment.
content_ideas: Tutorial: Build a multi-source research agent that routes questions to academic papers (vector store), web (Tavily), and relational DB (company wiki); compare retrieval quality across sources.
Case Study: Evaluate corrective RAG vs. adaptive RAG vs. basic RAG on domain-specific Q&A (e.g., medical, legal, technical docs). Measure latency, accuracy, token cost.
Deep Dive: LangGraph state machine design patterns for RAG; when to use conditional edges vs. agents vs. chains.
Benchmark: Compare embedding models (OpenAI, Cohere, open-source) on retrieval quality and latency for domain-specific indexes.
Tool Integration: Extend adaptive RAG to handle multi-turn conversations with memory windowing + routing + grading.
Middleware Patterns: Custom middleware for PII redaction, rate limiting, model fallback, cost tracking in RAG pipelines.
Step-Back Prompting Ablation: Test step-back on conceptual vs. factual questions; measure retrieval improvement on each.
HyDE Variants: Test HyDE with different hypothetical document prompts (paper, email, Wikipedia article, tweet) on same corpus; measure retrieval quality.
Query Decomposition Variants: Sequential (pass prior answers) vs. parallel (answer all independently) on multi-step reasoning tasks.
Routing Accuracy: Evaluate logical routing (LLM classification) vs. semantic routing (embedding similarity) on domain boundary cases.
Cost Optimization: Sweep window size K in ConversationalBufferWindowMemory; plot token cost vs. context quality on long conversations.
Fallback Mechanism Testing: Inject retrieval failures; verify web search + retry logic maintains end-user QA quality.
